title: Calculating Health Inequality in Complex Surveys
text: Analyzing health inequalities—concentration childhood malnutrition among poorest wealth quintiles—critical component global health research. However, calculating standardized metrics like Concentration Index using data complex, multi-stage stratified cluster surveys (DHS MICS) methodologically challenging. SurveyNCD package, developed StatAid Research Lab, provides streamlined, mathematically rigorous pipeline automate calculations. vignette demonstrates process raw anthropometric data calculate survey-weighted health inequality metrics just lines code.

title: Calculating Health Inequality in Complex Surveys

code: library(SurveyNCD) library(dplyr) library(srvyr)

title: Calculating Health Inequality in Complex Surveys
text: Raw survey datasets often store Z-scores integers (e.g., -254 instead -2.54) use specific numerical flags (like 9999) indicate missing biologically implausible data. Failing account flags severely distort means indices. who_anthro_score() function automatically cleans values categorizes according strict child growth standards.
code: # Simulating raw survey data with a missing flag (9999) raw_survey_data <- tibble(   cluster_id = c(1, 1, 2, 2),   strata = c(1, 1, 2, 2),   sample_weight = c(1.2, 0.8, 1.1, 0.9),   wealth_score = c(-1.5, -0.2, 0.5, 1.8),   raw_hw70 = c(-310, -254, 50, 9999) # Raw Height-for-Age )  # Apply the SurveyNCD cleaning function cleaned_data <- raw_survey_data %>%   mutate(     stunting_category = who_anthro_score(raw_hw70, indicator = "stunting"),     is_stunted = case_when(       stunting_category %in% c("Severe stunting", "Moderate stunting") ~ 1,       stunting_category == "Normal stunting" ~ 0,       TRUE ~ NA_real_     )   )  cleaned_data %>% select(raw_hw70, stunting_category, is_stunted) #> # A tibble: 4 × 3 #>   raw_hw70 stunting_category is_stunted #>      <dbl> <fct>                  <dbl> #> 1     -310 Severe stunting            1 #> 2     -254 Moderate stunting          1 #> 3       50 Normal stunting            0 #> 4     9999 NA                        NA

title: Survey-weighted concentration index — survey_concentration_index
text: standard concentration index $$C = \frac{2}{\mu} \mathrm{cov}_w(y_i, R_i),$$ \(\mu\) weighted mean \(y\) \(R_i\) weighted fractional rank: mid-point respondent's interval cumulative weight distribution (Lerman Yitzhaki 1989). Respondents tied ranking variable share mid-point tied group's interval, results depend order data. index slope \(\beta\) "convenient regression" Kakwani, Wagstaff van Doorslaer (1997), \(2\sigma_R^2 \, h(y_i) = \alpha + \beta R_i + \varepsilon_i\), fitted survey::svyglm() standard error design-based. bounds \(\le y \le b\) (O'Donnell et al. 2016): "CI" (standard): \(h(y) = y/\mu\). "generalized": \(h(y) = y\), giving \(\mu C\). "erreygers": \(h(y) = 4y/(b - )\), giving \(4\mu C/(b-)\) (Erreygers 2009). "wagstaff": \(h(y) = (b - )y/((b - \mu)(\mu - ))\), giving \((b-)\mu C/((b-\mu)(\mu-))\); binary outcomes \(C/(1-\mu)\) (Wagstaff 2005). bounded outcomes binary indicators Erreygers Wagstaff index usually preferred. standard error treats ranks \(\mu\) fixed.
